about: Plan for Scripts/release_tour.py. Every number the script uses that is not read from
SourceAssets/tour-review/tour-stops.json is here, so a human can review the plan before it runs.
The stop coordinates themselves are NOT duplicated here: they live in tour-stops.json,
which is also what AMikdashTourGuide loads at run time and what
Plugins/MikdashRuntime/Tests/TourMathTest.cpp mirrors. Three consumers, one set of numbers.
A thin disc on the floor under each stop. Deliberately content-free: the first mesh
in meshCandidates that loads is used. /Engine/BasicShapes is engine content that a
map referencing it will cook, so it needs nothing added to the project.
triangles is null on purpose - this script cannot verify a triangle count it was
never told, and asserting a guess would be worse than recording the real one.
If NO candidate loads the markers are omitted with evidence and the tour falls back
to its on-screen bearing and distance, which needs no asset at all.
Each marker's Z comes from a downward line trace at the stop's own XY. When the
trace misses, the Z written in tour-stops.json is used and the receipt records
which of the two produced each marker, per stop. The 2026-09-07 native route audit
against this map returned no hit for all 128 downward traces, so the fallback is the
expected path, not the exception - and the JSON Z values are themselves taken from
the architecture manifest's recorded floor tops.

Court of Israel at the player start

routeRules.about: Re-implementation of MikdashTour::Route::Validate in Python, checked offline against the JSON before anything is loaded. If these ever disagree with TourMath.h, TourMath.h is right.

limitations: Placement is geometric only. No visual, halachic, walking, collision-route or packaged acceptance is established by this script.
The walkability of the route between consecutive stops has NOT been verified by a native trace. Approach waypoints route the path through recorded gate and door openings on paper only.
The marker discs are wayfinding furniture, not part of the reconstruction. They are hidden on placement and the guide unhides only the current one at run time.
